title: Svelte components
description: For a Svelte interface: raw HTML blocks, effects kept for side effects, svelte-check in CI and accessibility warnings.

rules.instruction: Pass to `{@html ...}` only a string the application controls or has escaped; never render unsanitized content, such as text a user wrote, through it.
rules.verification: Search the change for `{@html` and check, for each one, where its string comes from and that a value from a user or an outside system is escaped or sanitized first.

rules.instruction: Compute a value from other state with `$derived` (or `$derived.by`), not by assigning state inside `$effect`; keep `$effect` for side effects such as analytics or direct DOM work.
rules.verification: Review each `$effect` the change adds and check that it does not assign state that `$derived` could compute.

rules.instruction: Install `svelte-check` as a development dependency and run it (`npx sv check` or `svelte-check`) in CI, so that type errors, unused CSS and accessibility hints of `.svelte` files fail the build.
rules.verification: task verify checks that a `package.json` names `svelte-check`; also check that CI runs it and that it reports no error on the change.

rules.instruction: Fix the accessibility warnings (`a11y_*`) the Svelte compiler reports; add a `<!-- svelte-ignore ... -->` comment only for a warning that is a false positive in that place, with the reason in parentheses.
rules.verification: Search the change for `svelte-ignore a11y` and check that each comment is on a false positive and states its reason.
